cohort: The abstract discusses pregnant patients with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) or those at risk, including overweight or obese patients.
finding: GDM is a common and increasing condition linked to maternal and fetal complications, but timely screening and management (lifestyle modifications, medication, and appropriate delivery timing) can reduce these risks, and continued postpartum care can mitigate the risk of developing overt diabetes.
mod_finding: GDM increases the risk of operative delivery, and recommendations for delivery include considering prelabor cesarean delivery for estimated fetal weight over 4,500g and delivering between 39/0 to 40/6 weeks of gestation (lifestyle controlled) or 39/0 to 39/6 weeks (medication controlled) for optimal outcomes.
gest_age: First-trimester (screening), 32 weeks (fetal surveillance start), 39/0 to 40/6 weeks (delivery range for lifestyle controlled GDM), 39/0 to 39/6 weeks (delivery range for medication controlled GDM)
